label: Acts 11:1
text: Now the apostles and the brothers who were in Judea heard that the Gentiles had also received the word of God.

label: Acts 11:2
text: When Peter had come up to Jerusalem, those who were of the circumcision contended with him,

label: Acts 11:3
text: saying, “You went in to uncircumcised men, and ate with them!”

label: Acts 11:4
text: But Peter began, and explained to them in order, saying,

label: Acts 11:5
text: “I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: a certain container descending, like it was a great sheet let down from heaven by four corners. It came as far as me.

label: Acts 11:6
text: When I had looked intently at it, I considered, and saw the four-footed animals of the earth, wild animals, creeping things, and birds of the sky.

label: Acts 11:7
text:
I also heard a voice saying to me,
‘Rise, Peter, kill and eat!’

label: Acts 11:8
text: But I said, ‘Not so, Lord, for nothing unholy or unclean has ever entered into my mouth.’

label: Acts 11:9
text:
But a voice answered me the second time out of heaven,
‘What God has cleansed, don’t you call unclean.’

label: Acts 11:10
text: This was done three times, and all were drawn up again into heaven.

label: Acts 11:11
text: Behold, immediately three men stood before the house where I was, having been sent from Caesarea to me.

label: Acts 11:12
text: The Spirit told me to go with them, without discriminating. These six brothers also accompanied me, and we entered into the man’s house.

variants.note: Wikipedia, Papyrus 45, Some notable readings: 'Acts 11:12 μηδὲν διακρίναντα (making no distinction): Omit.: 𝔓45 D it l p* syr h'. The WEB prints 'without discriminating'.

label: Acts 11:13
text: He told us how he had seen the angel standing in his house, and saying to him, ‘Send to Joppa, and get Simon, who is called Peter,

label: Acts 11:14
text: who will speak to you words by which you will be saved, you and all your house.’

label: Acts 11:15
text: As I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell on them, even as on us at the beginning.

label: Acts 11:16
text:
I remembered the word of the Lord, how he said,
‘John indeed baptized in water, but you will be baptized in the Holy Spirit.’

label: Acts 11:17
text: If then God gave to them the same gift as us, when we believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I, that I could withstand God?”

label: Acts 11:18
text: When they heard these things, they held their peace, and glorified God, saying, “Then God has also granted to the Gentiles repentance to life!”

label: Acts 11:19
text: They therefore who were scattered abroad by the oppression that arose about Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except to Jews only.

label: Acts 11:20
text: But there were some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who, when they had come to Antioch, spoke to the Hellenists, preaching the Lord Jesus.

label: Acts 11:21
text: The hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord.

label: Acts 11:22
text: The report concerning them came to the ears of the assembly which was in Jerusalem. They sent out Barnabas to go as far as Antioch,

label: Acts 11:23
text: who, when he had come, and had seen the grace of God, was glad. He exhorted them all, that with purpose of heart they should remain near to the Lord.

label: Acts 11:24
text: For he was a good man, and full of the Holy Spirit and of faith, and many people were added to the Lord.

label: Acts 11:25
text: Barnabas went out to Tarsus to look for Saul.

label: Acts 11:26
text: When he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. For a whole year they were gathered together with the assembly, and taught many people. The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch.

label: Acts 11:27
text: Now in these days, prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.

label: Acts 11:28
text: One of them named Agabus stood up, and indicated by the Spirit that there should be a great famine all over the world, which also happened in the days of Claudius.

label: Acts 11:29
text: As any of the disciples had plenty, each determined to send relief to the brothers who lived in Judea;

label: Acts 11:30
text: which they also did, sending it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul.

label: Circumcision was the communal boundary; eating with the uncircumcised provoked contention
statement: 'Those of the circumcision' contended with Peter because he went in to uncircumcised men and ate with them - circumcision as the boundary of the Jewish community, table-fellowship across it as a serious breach.
note: The same boundary as claim:ac-10-28-gentile-avoidance, now inside the church.

label: Believers scattered after Stephen's death preached in Phoenicia, Cyprus and Antioch
statement: Believers scattered by the oppression about Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus and Antioch, at first speaking only to Jews; men of Cyprus and Cyrene came to Antioch and spoke to Greeks (Hellenists), preaching the Lord Jesus.
note: The first reported preaching to non-Jews by nameless missionaries; no external evidence.

label: The Jerusalem church sent Barnabas to Antioch
statement: The report came to the Jerusalem assembly, which sent Barnabas as far as Antioch; he exhorted them all to remain near the Lord (11:22-23).

label: Barnabas went to Tarsus to find Saul and brought him to Antioch
statement: Barnabas went out to Tarsus to look for Saul; when he found him he brought him to Antioch, where they taught the assembly for a whole year (11:25-26).
note: Saul's move from Tarsus to Antioch; no external evidence.

label: Followers of Jesus were called 'Christians' (Christianoi)
statement: The disciples bore the name 'Christianoi' - the name by which adherents of the movement were known to outsiders.
note: Graded on the name's existence and use, not on its Antioch origin (split below).

label: The name 'Christian' was first given to the disciples in Antioch
statement: The disciples were first called Christians in Antioch - Antioch on the Orontes as the place where the name originated.
note: No independent source records the name's origin; even the supportive modern summary rests on this verse.

label: Prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch
statement: In those days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch, among them Agabus (11:27-28).
note: Itinerant prophets in the 40s; no external evidence.

label: Agabus predicted by the Spirit a great famine
statement: Agabus stood up and indicated by the Spirit that a great famine was coming over all the world.
note: A prediction: evidence can attest the famine it points to, never the prediction itself. Recorded as such; none-found.

label: A great famine occurred in the days of Claudius, reaching Judea
statement: A great famine occurred in the days of Claudius (c. 41-54 CE) and reached Judea; Acts 11:28 says 'over all the world' (the oikoumene).
note: Acts's 'all over the world' is wider than the Judean famine the sources document; the Rome grain crises show empire-wide shortage, not the Judean event.

label: The Antioch disciples sent relief to the brothers in Judea by Barnabas and Saul
statement: The Antioch disciples determined, each according to his means, to send relief to the brothers living in Judea, and sent it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul (11:29-30).
note: No source attests this relief mission; Josephus attests a parallel act of famine relief for Judea in the same period (Helena of Adiabene).

label: The Jerusalem community was led by elders who received the relief
statement: The relief was delivered to the elders of the Jerusalem community - elders as its recognized leadership.
note: No external evidence for the church's elders.
